children.cond: Pallor, dark (tea-colored) urine, breathlessness or rapid heart rate

pill.text: Emergency department now: acute hemolysis — CBC, reticulocytes, DAT, bilirubin, urinalysis

children.cond: Hemolysis with a negative direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test and jaundice in a sick child

pill.text: Think acute Wilson disease (low ALP is a clue): INR now; call hepatology / transplant center now

children.cond: Known Crigler–Najjar with fever, vomiting or fasting

pill.text: Same-day bilirubin and albumin; call hepatology today — risk of kernicterus

children.text: Fractionate: total and direct (or conjugated) bilirubin. Know which method your lab runs.
Hemolyzed sample? It lowers the measured direct bilirubin. Redraw rather than reassure.
AST and LDH also rise with hemolysis; ALP is high in growing children — read it against age norms.

children.cond: Direct or conjugated above the lab's range, or ALT or GGT raised
children.subtext: Not isolated unconjugated — follow Elevated Transaminases

children.cond: Pale stools, or dark urine with bilirubin on dipstick

children.text: CBC with reticulocytes, blood film, LDH, haptoglobin, direct antiglobulin test (DAT); glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) activity (First contact).

children.cond: Anemia, high reticulocytes or LDH, low haptoglobin

pill.text: Hematology: G6PD deficiency, hereditary spherocytosis, sickle cell disease, immune hemolysis

children.text: Chronic hemolysis with right upper quadrant pain or fever: think pigment gallstones — ultrasound.
Atazanavir inhibits UGT1A1 and raises unconjugated bilirubin — most visibly in Gilbert (UGT1A1*28/*28).
Fasting, fever, hard exercise or recent illness can double a Gilbert bilirubin — so can surgery or ICU stay.

children.subtext: Repeat when well and eating normally

children.text: Unconjugated, mean 2.8 ± 1.1 mg/dL (Maruo 2016) — usually below 5 mg/dL (expert opinion); CBC, reticulocytes and liver enzymes normal.

pill.text: Gilbert syndrome: reassure, stop testing; no genetic test needed. Record it for future drugs (irinotecan, atazanavir)

children.text: Persistently > 5 mg/dL when well, or jaundice since infancy (expert opinion).

pill.text: Hepatology: UGT1A1 sequencing (not the TA-repeat test alone); phenobarbital trial only under hepatology (Crigler–Najjar type II)

children.text: Liver test norms for age: see Age-Based Liver Test Norms.
